title: Why You See Afterimages After Staring at Bright Colours
hook: Stare at a strong colour, and you will see a different one.

narration.text: Stare at a strong colour, and you will see a different one.
This is an afterimage, and it is caused by your eyes adjusting.
The cells in your eyes, called cones, get tired after prolonged stimulation.
For example, staring at red makes the red-sensitive cones less responsive.
When you look away, the other cones are still fresh and active.
This temporary imbalance creates the illusion of the opposite colour.
Try it with a bright blue object, and then look at a white wall.
You will briefly see a yellow-orange afterimage on the wall.
Have you ever noticed this surprising effect in your own vision?

description: Ever wondered why you sometimes see a ghost image after staring at a bright colour? It is an optical illusion called an afterimage, and it is all about how your eye's cells respond to light. Learn the fascinating science behind this common visual trick.
topic: Why you sometimes see an optical illusion after staring at a strong colour, explaining afterimages.
